blockMcqs.question: What is this Tic-Tac-Toe LLD mainly testing?
blockMcqs.explanation: The interviewer grades how cleanly responsibilities split across classes and whether the design survives new requirements, not how well you play.

blockMcqs.question: Which requirement most tests extensibility?
blockMcqs.explanation: A configurable board size forces you to avoid hardcoding 3x3 anywhere in Board or the win-check logic.

blockMcqs.question: Which class should own turn orchestration?
blockMcqs.explanation: Game coordinates whose turn it is and when the match ends; Board only manages the grid itself.

blockMcqs.question: Why use an enum for X/O instead of strings?
blockMcqs.explanation: An enum restricts values to X or O at compile time, preventing typos like "x " that a raw string would silently allow.

blockMcqs.question: What makes Board support any N x N size?
blockMcqs.explanation: Board stores size as an instance field and builds its grid and counters off it, so N x N needs no code changes.

blockMcqs.question: In the Game loop, who decides the actual move?
blockMcqs.explanation: Game only asks the current player for a move via getMove(); the player (through its strategy) decides what that move is.

blockMcqs.question: Why check only the last move's row/col/diagonal?
options: Only those lines could have just completed
blockMcqs.explanation: A line can only become a winning line the instant its last empty cell is filled, so only lines through the newest move matter.

blockMcqs.question: What is the time complexity of the counter-based win check?
blockMcqs.explanation: Each move updates a fixed number of counters and checkWin only compares a few values, independent of board size.

blockMcqs.question: Why pull move selection into a PlayerStrategy?
options: So human and AI logic don't branch inside Player
blockMcqs.explanation: Delegating decideMove() to a strategy interface removes any if-human-else-AI branch from Player entirely.

blockMcqs.question: Which pattern lets Player swap between human and AI logic?
blockMcqs.explanation: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable move-selection algorithms behind one interface, decideMove(), plugged into Player.

blockMcqs.question: What mainly changes when extending to Connect-Four?
blockMcqs.explanation: Connect-Four reuses Board, Cell, and Player; only how a move lands (gravity drop) and win conditions differ.

blockMcqs.question: Why check win before checking for a full board?
options: A winning last move could be masked as a draw
blockMcqs.explanation: If the board fills on the winning move, checking fullness first would wrongly declare a draw instead of a win.
